The AP account supports a factual description of an unconventional, scrutinized public-information effort. It does not show that officials launched a television surrogate campaign to divert attention from Epstein-related scrutiny, so that motive is omitted here.

Trump cited Iran’s nuclear ambitions, development of long-range missiles and support for armed groups as reasons for the military action. He referred to earlier U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities and said the new campaign would target Iran’s missile and naval capabilities and its ability to support regional armed groups.

The address also included a direct appeal to members of Iran’s armed forces to surrender and to Iranian citizens to remain safe during the attacks and take control of their government. These are the stated rationales and appeals documented in the address. They support a factual account of what Trump said and announced. Establishing that this rhetoric conflicted with an anti-forever-war campaign brand would require separate, attributable campaign statements and context; the speech text alone does not demonstrate that comparison.
